name: deepseek-rate-card
note: Two readers, one card: the TypeScript lanes load this file through packages/eval/src/cost.ts and the tau2 driver loads it through eval/drivers/tau2/run_split.py. Both were hardcoded once and both were hardcoded separately, which is the arrangement in which one of them is eventually wrong. A test asserts the TypeScript constant matches this file, and a Python self-check asserts the driver's bill matches it too. One card per provider, one price row per model: the peak predicate belongs to the provider and the numbers belong to the model, which is how the provider publishes them. A run that names a model `prices` does not hold is billed at `defaultModel` and says so in its own artefact (`pricing.matches: false`, `pricing.pricedAs`), because an approximation that names itself is a number with an assumption and an approximation that does not is a number presented as a fact.
scheduling: A run scheduled inside a peak window pays exactly double, and a cron expression is a dispatch that nobody re-reads. The weekly regression run therefore starts at 18:00 UTC, which is outside the windows above and also outside the provider's published discount boundary, so the choice survives a correction to either one.
